source.title: NAIS-Net: Stable Deep Networks from Non-Autonomous Differential Equations
source.authors: Marco Ciccone; Marco Gallieri; Jonathan Masci; Christian Osendorfer; Faustino Gomez

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether enforcing stability changes the train–test generalization gap, using a different intervention from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classification results for NAIS-Net and ResNet, and explicitly reports a reduced CIFAR-10 generalization gap. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, fully connected versus convolutional networks, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study compares a stability-constrained residual architecture with ResNet. Its results address input-output stability and generalization gaps, but none tests V1–V8. Input-perturbation stability is not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, and fully connected MNIST experiments versus convolutional CIFAR experiments do not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: enforcing stability improves robustness and reduces the generalization gap without harming performance. Qualify this as their interpretation: the explicit 33% reduction concerns CIFAR-10 loss, while the table reports slightly lower mean test accuracies for NAIS-Net than ResNet.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a non-autonomous residual architecture with shared weights and a stability-enforcing reprojection procedure; compares it experimentally with ResNet.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100) and NAIS-Net unroll depth; the reported gap reduction is specifically for CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: NAIS-Net reportedly reduces the CIFAR-10 train–test loss gap by 33% relative to ResNet while achieving similar classification accuracy. The accuracy gaps themselves are approximately 8.14, 8.13, and 8.25 percentage points for ResNet, NAIS-Net 1, and NAIS-Net 10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A stability-constrained non-autonomous residual architecture can reduce the train–test loss gap while retaining comparable test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100, NAIS-Net 10 achieves 66.07% test accuracy versus 65.00% for NAIS-Net 1 and 66.34% for ResNet, with substantially lower training accuracy than ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional shared-weight unrolling can improve NAIS-Net test accuracy, and its stability-constrained architecture can reduce training fit while retaining comparable test accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: The reported CIFAR results are averaged over 5 runs, but the generalization-gap reduction is stated only for CIFAR-10 and no uncertainty for that reduction is given. The supplied results table is flattened.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied table supports the extracted numeric assignments. No verdicts apply because none of the eight versions is tested. The stability intervention also changes architecture and weight sharing, so the comparison does not isolate stability alone.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, decay, or switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adjusted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
